academic.title: ACADEMIC AMERICAN ENCYCLOPEDIA
records: Electronic machine that accepts data, performs stored instructions, and produces results. Personal computers commonly combine a microprocessor, semiconductor memory, disk storage, display, and keyboard.
Modulator-demodulator used to carry digital information over telephone circuits. Bell-compatible and Hayes-command-compatible equipment is common in personal computing.
Central processing unit formed on one or a few integrated circuits. Important families include the Intel 8086 and 80386, Motorola 68000, and MOS Technology 6502.
Region of the southern Caucasus with a long cultural history. The Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic formed part of the USSR in 1988.
International organization founded in 1945 to maintain peace, encourage cooperation, and address economic, social, and humanitarian questions.
Periodic comet returning to the inner solar system roughly every 76 years. Spacecraft and ground observatories studied its 1986 passage.
Loss of electrical resistance below a material's critical temperature. Ceramic compounds discovered in the 1980s greatly raised known transition temperatures.
Method of transmitting digital messages over amateur radio using framed packets, error checking, and terminal-node controllers.
Optical disc read by a laser. Audio compact discs store digitally encoded sound; related formats can distribute computer databases.
Warming produced when atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation. Scientists study how industrial emissions may alter climate.
Association of Western European states pursuing economic cooperation and a common market, with further integration planned for 1992.
Reusable United States spacecraft system consisting of an orbiter, external tank, and solid-fuel boosters. Flights resumed in 1988 after a lengthy suspension.
Second-largest continent, extending across the equator and containing great geographic, linguistic, and cultural diversity.
Ice-covered continent surrounding the South Pole, administered for peaceful scientific use under the Antarctic Treaty.
Description of matter as elements composed of atoms with nuclei of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Design, operation, and history of heavier-than-air flight, including civil transport, military aircraft, and general aviation.
Federal nation occupying northern North America, composed in 1988 of ten provinces and two territories.
East Asian nation with an ancient civilization and the world's largest population in the late twentieth century.
Legal and political protections intended to ensure equal treatment and participation in public life.
Orbiting relay that receives, amplifies, and retransmits telephone, television, and data signals.
Fundamental law adopted in 1787 establishing the federal government and allocation of its powers.
Deoxyribonucleic acid, the hereditary material whose nucleotide sequence carries genetic information in living organisms.
Ground motion produced by sudden release of strain in Earth's crust, commonly along geological faults.
Phenomena associated with electric charge, current, voltage, resistance, and electromagnetic fields.
Western European republic whose capital is Paris, noted for major contributions to politics, art, science, and literature.
Central European region divided in 1988 between the Federal Republic of Germany and German Democratic Republic.
Severe worldwide economic contraction beginning in 1929 and continuing through much of the 1930s.
South Asian federal republic whose varied regions include the Himalayas, Indo-Gangetic plain, and Deccan plateau.
Transformation beginning in eighteenth-century Britain through mechanized production, factories, and new power sources.
Electronic circuit containing transistors and other components formed together on semiconductor material.
East Asian island nation with a constitutional monarchy and a highly developed industrial economy.
Device producing a narrow, coherent beam through stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.
Federal republic south of the United States with a cultural heritage drawing on Indigenous and Spanish traditions.
Earth's natural satellite, orbiting at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometers and influencing ocean tides.
Defensive alliance formed in 1949 by the United States, Canada, and Western European nations.
Continuous body of salt water covering most of Earth and divided conventionally into major ocean basins.
Production of durable images by recording light on sensitized film or electronic imaging devices.
Theory that Earth's outer shell consists of moving plates responsible for many earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain ranges.
System using reflected radio waves to determine the direction, distance, or speed of objects.
Transmission and reception of information using electromagnetic waves, including broadcasting and two-way communication.
Period of European cultural and intellectual renewal conventionally associated with the fourteenth through sixteenth centuries.
Engineering field concerned with programmable machines capable of sensing and performing physical tasks.
Federal socialist state spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia, composed of fifteen union republics in 1988.
System converting sound into electrical signals for transmission between distant locations through switched networks.
Transmission and display of moving images and sound using radio-frequency, cable, or related electronic systems.
Semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electrical signals and a basic element of modern electronic circuits.
State comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, governed as a constitutional monarchy.
Conflict involving North and South Vietnam and international forces, ending with reunification in 1975.
Global conflict of 1914-1918 centered in Europe and involving the Allied and Central Powers.
Global conflict of 1939-1945 between the Axis powers and Allies, transforming international politics and society.

medical.title: MEDICAL INFORMATION
records: Viral upper-respiratory infection commonly causing congestion, sore throat, and cough. Antibiotics do not treat viruses. Persistent or severe symptoms require professional evaluation.
Acute viral respiratory illness often accompanied by fever, aches, and fatigue. Vaccination recommendations vary by age and risk group.
Persistently elevated blood pressure can increase the risk of heart, kidney, and vascular disease. Diagnosis requires properly performed repeated measurements.
Group of disorders characterized by impaired regulation of blood glucose. Management may include diet, monitoring, medication, and insulin under medical supervision.
Cool a minor thermal burn with clean cool water and protect it with a sterile covering. Extensive, deep, electrical, or facial burns require prompt emergency care.
Apply direct pressure with clean material. Severe or uncontrolled bleeding is an emergency requiring immediate professional assistance.
Loss of water and salts may follow heat, illness, or inadequate intake. Confusion, faintness, or inability to retain fluids warrants prompt medical care.
Allergies range from localized irritation to a rapid life-threatening reaction. Breathing difficulty or collapse requires emergency assistance.
Waxy substance transported in blood lipoproteins and used by the body. Elevated levels of some fractions are associated with cardiovascular risk.
Medicines used against susceptible bacteria. They do not cure viral infections, and selection and duration should be directed by a clinician.
Diagnostic technique using magnetic fields and radio-frequency signals to construct images without ionizing x-rays.
Suspected poisoning requires immediate advice from a poison-control center or emergency service. Do not induce vomiting unless specifically instructed.
Abdominal discomfort has many possible causes. Severe, persistent, localized, or accompanied symptoms require professional assessment.
Condition in which blood has reduced oxygen-carrying capacity, commonly associated with low hemoglobin or red-cell abnormalities.
Inflammation of the appendix may cause increasing abdominal pain, nausea, and fever and requires urgent medical evaluation.
General term for joint inflammation or degeneration causing pain, stiffness, swelling, or reduced movement.
Condition involving episodic narrowing and inflammation of airways, often producing wheezing, cough, and shortness of breath.
Back pain may arise from muscle strain, joints, discs, nerves, or other disease; weakness or bladder changes require urgent care.
Inflammation of bronchial airways commonly causing cough and mucus production; causes may be infectious or irritant-related.
Clouding of the eye's lens that can progressively reduce vision and may be treated surgically.
Contagious viral illness characterized by fever and an itchy blistering rash, particularly common in children in 1988.
Brain injury after a blow or rapid movement; confusion, repeated vomiting, worsening headache, or unconsciousness requires emergency attention.
Narrowing of arteries supplying the heart may produce angina or heart attack and is associated with several modifiable risks.
Inflammation of skin producing redness, itching, scaling, or blisters, with allergic, irritant, and other possible causes.
Infection or inflammation of the outer or middle ear may cause pain, fever, drainage, or temporary hearing difficulty.
Disorder characterized by recurrent seizures resulting from abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
Elevated body temperature is commonly a response to infection; very high, persistent, or concerning fever requires medical advice.
Broken bone may cause pain, swelling, deformity, or loss of function and should be immobilized pending professional care.
Group of eye diseases capable of damaging the optic nerve, sometimes associated with elevated pressure inside the eye.
Headache has many causes; sudden severe pain or pain with neurological symptoms, fever, or injury needs prompt evaluation.
Loss of blood supply damaging heart muscle may cause chest pressure, sweating, nausea, or breathlessness and is an emergency.
Inflammation of the liver caused by viruses, toxins, medicines, or other disorders and sometimes producing jaundice.
Administration of a vaccine to stimulate protection against a particular infectious disease.
Hard mineral deposits in the urinary tract may cause intense flank pain, nausea, or blood in urine.
Highly contagious viral disease causing fever, cough, and widespread rash; complications can be serious.
Recurring neurological disorder often producing throbbing headache, nausea, and sensitivity to light or sound.
Infection or inflammation of lung tissue that may cause fever, cough, chest discomfort, and difficult breathing.
Injury to ligaments surrounding a joint, often causing pain, swelling, and reduced movement.
Interruption of brain blood supply or bleeding may cause sudden weakness, speech difficulty, or vision change and is an emergency.
Skin injury from ultraviolet radiation; extensive blistering, fever, or dehydration warrants medical attention.
Serious nervous-system illness caused by toxin-producing bacteria entering wounds and preventable through immunization.
Neck gland producing hormones that influence metabolism, growth, temperature regulation, and other functions.
Inflammation of the tonsils commonly producing sore throat and painful swallowing, with viral or bacterial causes.
Infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, usually affecting lungs and requiring prolonged combination treatment.
Break in skin or mucosal tissue; peptic ulcers affect the stomach or duodenum and may cause pain or bleeding.
Microbial infection of urinary structures may cause burning, frequency, urgency, fever, or flank pain.
Medical name for chickenpox, a contagious viral infection marked by successive crops of itchy blisters.
Tests of visual acuity and eye function can identify refractive errors and signs needing comprehensive examination.
Minor wounds should be cleaned and protected; deep, contaminated, bitten, or poorly healing wounds need medical evaluation.
Diagnostic use of penetrating ionizing radiation to form images, especially of bones, lungs, and certain internal structures.

library.title: ELECTRONIC LIBRARY
records: A practical guide to OK, CONNECT, BUSY, NO CARRIER, and NO DIALTONE responses, with suggestions for checking dialing commands and telephone connections.
Keep a bootable diskette, record the original file, change one driver at a time, and verify available conventional memory after every restart.
IBM-compatible systems commonly use IRQ 4 for COM1 and IRQ 3 for COM2. Additional ports or devices may conflict unless adapters are reconfigured.
Match diskette density to the drive, protect media from magnets and heat, label it clearly, and retain more than one backup copy.
A terminal-node controller assembles characters into checked packets for transmission over amateur-radio channels.
Assign realistic application partitions, limit unnecessary startup documents, and retain enough free memory for the System and temporary allocations.
Confirm monitor timing, adapter switches, application modes, and available drivers before replacing a working display configuration.
Prepare searches offline, capture long results, use GO commands, and schedule large transfers during lower-rate hours.
Shareware may be copied for evaluation under the author's stated terms. Continued use generally calls for registration and payment.
Copy irreplaceable files before running diagnostics or changing disk-controller parameters. Verify that backup media can be read.
Reports commonly state temperature, conditions, wind direction and speed, and a short forecast. Local conditions can change rapidly.
Browse descriptions before downloading, note the file number and size, select a supported transfer protocol, and read accompanying documentation.
Keep startup commands readable, document resident programs, and test changes one line at a time.
Remove extension devices, listen for noise, try another cord, and compare local and long-distance calls before blaming a modem.
Name captures by service and date, review them offline, and remove control characters before printing.
CGA, EGA, and VGA provide different resolutions, colors, monitor requirements, and compatibility modes.
Compare command compatibility, error control, indicator lights, documentation, warranty, and serial-cable requirements.
Publish an agenda, arrange demonstrations, exchange public-domain files, and leave time for member questions.
Group applications logically, remove obsolete temporary files, and keep recovery copies before reorganizing disks.
Keep the paper path clean, replace worn ribbons, verify tractor alignment, and run the printer self-test.
Store frequently used numeric User IDs under recognizable names and verify the resolved recipient before sending.
Confirm switch settings, cable type, monitor compatibility, and software mode before operating a replacement adapter.
Match protocols at both ends, disable unwanted flow control, and verify that no terminal program translates binary data.
Stop writing to a damaged diskette, make a sector copy when possible, and work only on the duplicate.
Use descriptive subjects, quote only necessary lines, identify equipment clearly, and report the final solution.
Maintain several dated backup sets and keep at least one copy away from the computer.
AT tests attention, ATZ resets, ATDT dials by tone, ATH hangs up, and ATS0 controls automatic answer.
Common assignments include IRQ 3 for COM2, IRQ 4 for COM1, IRQ 6 for floppy control, and IRQ 7 for printing.
CD-ROM distributes large read-only collections; access requires a compatible drive, interface, and retrieval software.
Follow charging instructions, avoid unnecessary backlighting, and carry saved work before battery voltage becomes low.
Save alternate versions, verify formulas after copying ranges, and print critical totals for comparison.
Keep a startup disk, allow desktop rebuilding to finish, and retain separate copies of valuable documents.
Software and hardware flow control prevent buffer overflow, but both endpoints must use compatible settings.
Search distinctive names or technical terms, note dates and sources, and distinguish current from period editions.
Compose mail offline, prepare GO destinations, and reserve large downloads for lower-rate hours.
Verify radio audio levels, TNC mode, call sign, serial speed, and a known-good terminal cable.
Choose a non-obvious password, do not share it, and avoid leaving it in terminal command files.
Protect unexposed and processed film from heat, moisture, chemical fumes, scratches, and prolonged bright light.
Choose the exact model when available or a documented compatible emulation, then test plain text before graphics.
Read distribution terms, scan accompanying documentation, and register shareware that remains in use.
Transmit, receive, ground, request-to-send, clear-to-send, carrier-detect, and terminal-ready signals coordinate serial devices.
Record current settings and jumper positions before changes, and keep a bootable diagnostic diskette available.
Assign unique device numbers, terminate both ends of the bus, and use suitable cable lengths and connectors.
Use correctly rated protective equipment, preserve ventilation, and shut down before electrical work.
Match columns, character format, control sequences, duplex, and flow control to the host service.
Preserve an original copy and account for line endings, tab widths, character sets, and printer control codes.
Select the proper library, provide an accurate description, state distribution terms, and await SysOp review.
Obtain software from known sources, retain write-protected originals, and investigate unexpected file changes.
Moisture, damaged cables, and storms may add noise; compare conditions and report persistent trouble to the telephone company.
Save dated copies before conversion or major editing and verify that backup documents reopen correctly.
